operations.specification: User registration endpoint for creating new user accounts in the Todo application. This operation creates a new user record with email and password, validates input, and issues initial authentication tokens. Associated with the todo_app_users table.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows new users to register for the Todo application by creating a user account with email and password credentials. The operation validates that the email format is correct and that the email is not already registered in the system. It enforces password complexity requirements including minimum length and character diversity. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new user record in the todo_app_users table with initial status set to 'active' and generates authentication tokens for immediate access.

The operation uses the email field for unique identification and stores the password securely using bcrypt hashing in the password_hash field. The created_at timestamp is automatically set to record the registration time. This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication, serving as the entry point for new users to join the Todo application.

Security considerations include preventing duplicate email registrations and ensuring proper password hashing before storage. The operation integrates with the authentication system to provide seamless transition from registration to authenticated session. Related operations include login for existing users and password reset functionality for account recovery.
operations.summary: Register a new user account for the Todo application

requestBody.description: User registration information including email and password

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user information upon successful registration

operations.name: join

operations.specification: User login endpoint for authenticating existing users in the Todo application. This operation validates user credentials against stored records and issues authentication tokens for session management. Associated with the todo_app_users table.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates existing users by validating their email and password credentials against the stored records in the todo_app_users table. The operation checks the email existence and verifies the provided password against the stored password_hash using bcrypt comparison. Upon successful authentication, it creates a new session record in todo_app_user_sessions with the user's IP address, connection URL, and referrer information.

The operation validates that the user account has an 'active' status in the status field before allowing login. It generates JWT access and refresh tokens with appropriate expiration times for secure session management. The created_at timestamp in the session record captures the login time, while the expired_at field remains null until session termination.

Security measures include rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks and proper error handling that doesn't reveal whether the email or password was incorrect. The operation integrates with the token refresh system to maintain continuous session management. Users who successfully authenticate gain access to their personal todo management functionality.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user information upon successful login

operations.specification: Token refresh endpoint for renewing authentication tokens in the Todo application. This operation validates refresh tokens and issues new access tokens without requiring re-authentication. Associated with the todo_app_user_sessions table.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows authenticated users to refresh their access tokens using a valid refresh token, extending their session without requiring full re-authentication. The operation validates the refresh token against the user's active session records in the todo_app_user_sessions table, ensuring it hasn't expired based on the expired_at field.

Upon successful validation, the system issues a new access token with updated expiration while maintaining the same user context. This operation helps maintain seamless user experience by preventing frequent login interruptions. The session record's created_at timestamp is used to track session duration for security monitoring.

Security considerations include proper token validation, prevention of token reuse, and session expiration enforcement. The operation supports the JWT-based authentication system by providing continuous access while maintaining security standards. It requires a valid refresh token from a previous successful authentication operation.

This endpoint allows users to initiate the password reset process by providing their registered email address. The operation validates that the email exists in the todo_app_users table and that the user account has an 'active' status. It generates a secure, time-limited reset token and sends it to the user's email address for verification.

The operation ensures that only active user accounts can request password resets and implements rate limiting to prevent abuse. It records the reset request for security auditing purposes but doesn't immediately change the password. The user must complete the verification process through the received email link to actually reset their password.

Security considerations include preventing email enumeration by providing generic success messages regardless of email existence, implementing secure token generation, and enforcing time limits on reset tokens. This operation is part of the comprehensive account recovery system for the Todo application.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing user information and tokens upon successful login or token refresh. This DTO provides the authenticated user's basic information along with JWT tokens for session management.

The response includes the user's unique identifier, email address, and authentication tokens required for accessing protected resources. The token field contains both access and refresh tokens with appropriate expiration times for secure session management.

This DTO represents the successful outcome of authentication operations and enables the client to maintain authenticated state while interacting with the Todo application's protected endpoints.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user from the todo_app_users table. This ID is used to associate todos and other user-specific data throughout the application.

email.description: Authenticated user's email address from the todo_app_users table. This email is used for user identification and communication purposes.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted. Null if account is active

ITodoAppUser.ILogin.description:
User authentication credentials for login operations.

This DTO contains the email and password combination required to authenticate a user against the Todo application. The email field must match a registered user account in the todo_app_users table, and the password must be validated against the stored password_hash.

For security purposes, this operation also requires session context information including the client's IP address, current connection URL (href), and referrer URL. These fields are used to create audit records in the todo_app_user_sessions table for security monitoring and compliance.

The system validates the credentials using secure password hashing algorithms and implements rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks. Failed authentication attempts are logged without revealing specific validation details to prevent information disclosure.

email.description: User's registered email address used for authentication. Must match an existing account in the todo_app_users table and pass email format validation.

password.description: User's password in plain text for authentication verification. The system validates this against the stored password_hash using secure hashing algorithms.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing. Used to create session records in todo_app_user_sessions table.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the login request originated. Required for session context and audit purposes.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) that directed the user to the login page. Used for session context and user journey tracking.

ITodoAppUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for extending user authentication sessions in the Todo application. This DTO contains the refresh token required to validate and renew authentication without requiring full re-authentication.

The refresh token must be a valid, non-expired token issued during a previous successful authentication operation. The system validates the token against active session records in the todo_app_user_sessions table and ensures it hasn't been revoked or expired based on the expired_at field.

Security considerations include proper token validation, prevention of token reuse, and enforcement of token expiration policies. Successful token refresh results in new access and refresh tokens being issued with updated expiration times.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token issued during previous authentication. This token is validated against the user's active session records to ensure it hasn't expired or been revoked. The token must be non-expired and properly signed.

The system performs cryptographic validation of the token signature and checks the expiration time against the current system time. If validation fails, the refresh operation is rejected.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthResponse.description:
Authentication response containing JWT tokens and user session information.

This DTO represents the successful authentication response returned after a user successfully logs into the Todo application. It includes the authenticated user's basic information along with JWT tokens for secure session management.

The response contains both access and refresh tokens to support secure authentication patterns. The user information includes the user ID and email for client-side session management, while excluding sensitive data like password_hash for security reasons.

Session context is established through the generated tokens, which are used for subsequent API requests to maintain authenticated state. The system tracks session information in the todo_app_user_sessions table for audit and security monitoring purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user from the todo_app_users table.

email.description: Authenticated user's email address for session context and display purposes.

token.description: JWT token information containing access and refresh tokens for secure session management.

ITodoAppUser.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a user for authentication responses and basic user information display. This DTO provides the essential user data required for client-side user identification while maintaining security by excluding sensitive information.

The summary includes the user's unique identifier, email address, account status, and timestamps which are sufficient for most client-side user management needs. This lightweight representation is used in authentication responses and other contexts where full user details are not required.

Security considerations ensure that sensitive fields like password_hash are excluded from this summary representation while maintaining essential account status information for proper user management throughout the application lifecycle.

id.description: User's unique identifier from the todo_app_users table. This ID is used throughout the application to associate data with the specific user and serves as the primary key for user account management.

email.description: User's email address used for authentication and communication. This email must be unique across all user accounts in the system and follows standard email format validation.

status.description: Current status of the user account from the todo_app_users table. Possible values: 'active', 'inactive', 'suspended'. This field indicates the operational state of the user account for access control purposes.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. This field provides account creation context and is used for chronological organization of user records.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated. This field tracks the most recent modification to the user account for audit and synchronization purposes.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted. Null if account is active. This field supports account recovery capabilities and data retention policies.

ITodoAppUser.IResetPasswordRequest.description:
Request body for initiating password reset process. This DTO contains the email address of the user requesting password reset along with session context information for security auditing.

The operation validates that the email exists in the todo_app_users table and that the user account has an 'active' status. It generates a secure, time-limited reset token and sends it to the user's email address for verification.

Security considerations include preventing email enumeration by providing generic success messages regardless of email existence, implementing secure token generation, and enforcing time limits on reset tokens. Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are required for comprehensive security auditing and compliance with authentication tracking requirements.

This operation ensures that only active user accounts can request password resets and implements rate limiting to prevent abuse of the password recovery system.

email.description:
Registered email address of the user requesting password reset. Must be a valid email format and exist in the todo_app_users table with an 'active' status.

The system validates this email against existing user accounts but provides generic success messages to prevent email enumeration attacks. If the email exists and the account is active, a secure reset token is generated and sent to this address.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing. Used to create session records in todo_app_user_sessions table for comprehensive security monitoring.

This field provides critical security information for tracking the geographic location and network origin of password reset requests, helping to identify suspicious patterns or unauthorized access attempts.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) where the password reset request originated. Required for session context and audit purposes.

Tracking the connection URL provides valuable context for security analysis and helps understand user navigation patterns during the password recovery process.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) that directed the user to the password reset page. Used for session context and user journey tracking.

This information supports security monitoring by identifying unusual referral patterns and contributes to understanding how users access the password recovery functionality.

ITodoAppUser.IResetPasswordResponse.description:
Response body confirming password reset request processing. This DTO provides a generic success message to prevent email enumeration attacks.

Regardless of whether the email exists in the system, this response is returned to maintain security by not revealing whether an email is registered. If the email exists and the account is active, a reset token is generated and sent via email.

The response includes a timestamp indicating when the reset request was processed for audit purposes. This DTO integrates with the todo_app_users table from the Prisma schema, supporting the password reset workflow while maintaining security best practices.

message.description:
Generic success message confirming that the password reset request has been processed. This message is intentionally vague to prevent email enumeration attacks.

Example: 'If the email address exists in our system, a password reset link has been sent.'

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset request was processed. Used for audit logging and rate limiting purposes.

This timestamp helps track reset request patterns and prevents abuse of the password reset functionality. May be null if processing is delayed.

user_id.description:
Unique identifier of the user account from the todo_app_users table. Used for audit trail and security monitoring.

This field is included when the email exists and the account is active, providing context for the reset operation without revealing sensitive information.

Unique identifier of the authenticated user from the todo_app_users table. This ID is used to verify authorization and ensure the password change applies to the correct account.

The system validates that this user_id matches the authenticated session to prevent unauthorized password changes.

current_password.description:
Current password for verification against the stored password_hash in the todo_app_users table. This field must match the user's existing password to authorize the password change operation.

The system validates this password by comparing it against the securely hashed password_hash stored in the database. If the current password does not match, the operation will fail with an authentication error.

This security measure prevents unauthorized password changes even if an attacker gains temporary access to a user's session.

new_password.description:
New password that will replace the current password after successful verification. This password must meet the same complexity requirements as during user registration.

The system will hash this password using secure cryptographic algorithms before storing it in the password_hash field of the todo_app_users table.

Password complexity requirements include minimum length, character variety, and other security standards to ensure account protection.

ITodoAppUser.IChangePassword.description:
Password change request DTO for authenticated users in the Todo application.

This schema defines the structure for changing a user's password while maintaining an active session. The operation requires verification of the current password to prevent unauthorized changes, ensuring that only the legitimate account owner can modify the password.

The DTO includes both the current password for verification and the new password that will replace it. Both fields undergo validation to ensure they meet security standards before processing the password change operation. This DTO integrates with the todo_app_users table from the Prisma schema, supporting secure password management workflows.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password change operation completed successfully. Returns true if the password was successfully updated, false if the operation failed.

This field provides immediate feedback to the client about the operation outcome, allowing for appropriate user interface responses.

message.description:
Descriptive message providing details about the password change operation result. For successful operations, this typically confirms the password change.

For failed operations, this message provides specific error information to help users understand what went wrong and how to correct it.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the password was successfully changed. This value corresponds to the updated_at field in the todo_app_users table.

This timestamp helps track security-related changes to user accounts and can be used for audit purposes or to inform users about recent account activity.

ITodoAppUser.IChangePasswordResponse.description:
Password change response DTO confirming the outcome of the password update operation.

This schema provides confirmation and details about the password change process. It includes success status, descriptive messaging, and timestamp information to ensure users receive comprehensive feedback about the security update.

The response helps maintain transparency about account security changes and provides necessary information for client-side handling of the password change operation.

ITodoAppConfiguration.description:
System-wide application configuration settings for the Todo application.

This entity stores key-value pairs for various application settings that can be modified by system administrators. Configuration changes are tracked with timestamps for audit purposes, and each setting includes data type information for proper validation and parsing.

The configuration system supports different data types including 'string', 'boolean', 'number', and 'json' formats, ensuring that configuration values are properly validated before being applied to the application. Each configuration setting requires a unique key identifier and a clear description of its purpose and impact on system behavior.

Configuration settings are global entities that don't require FK transformations as they are system-wide settings not owned by specific users or entities. They follow the proper standalone entity pattern with clear data type validation and status management.

ITodoAppConfiguration.ISummary.description:

The summary format balances information density with performance considerations, making it ideal for configuration management interfaces where users need to browse available settings before viewing or editing specific configuration values. The inclusion of the config_value field allows users to see the current setting value without needing to access the full configuration details.

This DTO supports efficient pagination and search operations while providing sufficient information for users to identify and select configuration settings for further action. It maintains consistency with the full ITodoAppConfiguration DTO while optimizing for performance in list views.

When creating configuration settings, administrators should provide clear descriptions that explain the purpose and impact of each setting, as this information helps other team members understand the configuration system and make informed changes when necessary. This DTO integrates with the todo_app_configurations table from the Prisma schema, incorporating all available configuration fields with proper validation.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and retrieving todo items with comprehensive search capabilities.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:

The creation operation validates the todo title to ensure it meets business requirements of 1-255 characters and contains valid content. Upon successful creation, the system automatically sets the initial status to 'active' and records the creation timestamp.

This DTO is used when authenticated users create new todo items within their personal todo list. The operation includes comprehensive error handling for validation failures.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Represents a todo item in the Todo application. Each todo belongs to a specific user and supports creation, completion, editing, and deletion workflows. Todos maintain their creation order and support soft deletion for data recovery capabilities.

The todo entity includes comprehensive status tracking with timestamps for creation, completion, and modification. Todos are validated for title length (1-255 characters) and content requirements before being stored in the system.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item designed for efficient display in lists and overviews. This DTO provides essential information for todo management while optimizing for performance in list views.

This summary type includes only the most critical fields needed for basic todo display, excluding detailed metadata that would be available in the full entity representation. It is particularly useful for paginated lists, search results, and dashboard overviews where performance and data transfer efficiency are important considerations.

The status field supports the core todo workflow, allowing users to track task completion progress. The completed_at timestamp provides valuable context about when work was finished, while the creation timestamp helps maintain chronological organization of tasks.

Including the user field provides essential ownership context without requiring additional API calls, ensuring complete information retrieval in single operations. This DTO integrates with the todo_app_todos Prisma schema, maintaining data consistency across the application.

ITodoAppTodo.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating existing todo items. This DTO contains only user-editable fields that can be modified by authenticated users after todo creation.

The update operation validates that the todo exists, belongs to the authenticated user, and that the update data meets business rules including title length constraints (1-255 characters) and valid status transitions. All fields in this DTO are optional, allowing users to update specific properties without modifying the entire todo item.

Security improvements include the removal of system-managed timestamp fields (updated_at, deleted_at) which should never be user-updatable. The completed_at field is managed automatically based on status changes to maintain data integrity.

This DTO integrates with the todo_app_todos Prisma schema and includes only the truly updatable fields from the underlying database model. The system automatically updates modification timestamps when changes are applied and enforces business rules for data integrity.

title.description: Updated todo item title/content. Must meet the same validation requirements as creation (1-255 characters and valid content). This field allows users to modify the task description while maintaining business rule compliance.

status.description:
Updated status of the todo item. Valid transitions include: 'active' to 'completed' and 'completed' to 'active'. When status changes to 'completed', the system automatically sets the completed_at timestamp. When changing from 'completed' to 'active', the completed_at is cleared.

The status field uses the ITodoAppTodoStatus enum for type safety and ensures only valid status values are accepted during updates. This field integrates with the status field in the todo_app_todos Prisma schema, ensuring data consistency across the application.

ITodoAppUserSession.description:
User session records for authentication tracking in the Todo application.

Each session represents an active login instance for a user and contains metadata used for audit tracing of user actions and secure session management. Sessions are created during user authentication and track connection details including IP address, URL context, and timing information.

The session lifecycle includes creation upon successful authentication, active usage period, and eventual expiration either through user logout, timeout due to inactivity, or administrative termination. Expired sessions maintain their records for audit purposes while preventing further authentication.

This entity integrates with the todo_app_user_sessions table from the Prisma schema, maintaining proper relationships with user accounts through the todo_app_user_id foreign key. Session records support security monitoring, compliance requirements, and user activity analysis throughout the application lifecycle.

ITodoAppUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a user session record designed for audit and monitoring purposes. This DTO provides essential session information for security tracking and user activity monitoring.

This summary type captures the key metadata associated with user authentication sessions, including connection details and timing information. It is particularly useful for security audits, user activity reports, and session management interfaces where detailed session information needs to be reviewed.

The IP address and referrer fields provide valuable security context, helping to identify suspicious patterns or unauthorized access attempts. The timing fields (created_at and expired_at) enable session duration analysis and help identify sessions that may require manual intervention or investigation.

This DTO supports compliance requirements by maintaining an audit trail of user authentication events and session lifecycle management. The schema aligns with the todo_app_user_sessions Prisma model which tracks user authentication sessions with detailed connection information for audit purposes.

oneOf.description:
Active status for todo items representing pending tasks that require user action. This status indicates that the todo item is currently awaiting completion and should be displayed prominently in user interfaces.

When a todo is created, it automatically receives the 'active' status by default. Active todos represent the user's current workload and are typically displayed in chronological order with the most recent items appearing first. The system maintains active todos until they are explicitly marked as completed by the user.

This status corresponds directly to the status field in the todo_app_todos Prisma schema, ensuring consistent status management throughout the application lifecycle. Business rules validate that todos can transition between 'active' and 'completed' states while maintaining data integrity.

Completed status for todo items representing finished tasks that have been accomplished by the user. This status indicates that the todo item no longer requires action and can be archived or filtered from active views.

When a user marks a todo as completed, the system automatically records the completion timestamp and updates the status accordingly. Completed todos are typically displayed in a separate section or can be filtered out to focus on active tasks. The system supports reactivation of completed todos if users need to revisit tasks.

This status corresponds directly to the status field in the todo_app_todos Prisma schema and includes automatic timestamp tracking for completion events. Business rules ensure that status transitions maintain proper data consistency and support the core todo management workflow.

ITodoAppTodoStatus.description:
Status enumeration for todo items representing their completion state within the Todo application. This enum defines the two possible states for todo items: 'active' for pending tasks and 'completed' for finished tasks.

The status system supports the core todo management workflow by providing clear state indicators for task tracking. Each status transition is validated by business rules to ensure data integrity and proper workflow management. The enum values correspond directly to the status field in the todo_app_todos Prisma schema, maintaining consistency between the database model and API contracts.

Status management includes automatic timestamp tracking for completion events and supports the filtering and organization capabilities that users expect from a modern todo application. The system ensures that todos maintain their state throughout their lifecycle while supporting the flexibility needed for effective task management.
